title: LEBER OPTIC ATROPHY AND DYSTONIA
alt_titles: LEBER HEREDITARY OPTIC NEUROPATHY WITH DYSTONIA
DYSTONIA, FAMILIAL, WITH VISUAL FAILURE AND STRIATAL LUCENCIES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in the mitochondrial MTND6 gene (516006) or the mitochondrial MTND4 gene (516003).

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in the mitochondrial MTND6 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract says LDYT is caused by mutations in ND6, which is MTND6.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in the mitochondrial MTND4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract says LDYT is caused by mutations in ND4, which is MTND4.

paragraphs.text: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder (Jun et al., 1994). Families with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia have been reported. In these families the generalized dystonia was attributed to striatal degeneration (Watanabe et al., 2006). The disorder is caused by mitochondrial DNA mutations in complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) subunit genes (De Vries et al., 1996). A mutation in the MTND6 gene has been suggested as the disease-causing mutation in several families (Watanabe et al., 2006).

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: A mitochondrial DNA mutation at nucleotide pair 14459 of the NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 gene associated with maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia.
checks.explanation: The title describes the disorder as maternally inherited and tied to an mtDNA mutation.

checks.claim: Families with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia have been reported.
checks.evidence_quote: has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
checks.explanation: The paper refers to previously reported families with LHON and/or dystonia.

checks.claim: In families with LHON and/or dystonia, the generalized dystonia was attributed to striatal degeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a Japanese family with generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, which occurred in childhood, and late-onset optic neuropathy.
checks.explanation: The paper attributes the dystonia to striatal degeneration only in this one Japanese family. The draft extends that attribution to the earlier LHON and/or dystonia families in general.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is caused by mitochondrial DNA mutations in complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) subunit genes.
checks.evidence_quote: Biochemical analysis of a muscle biopsy revealed a severe complex I deficiency, providing a link between these unique mtDNA mutations and this rare, complex phenotype including Leber optic neuropathy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports mutations in two complex I subunit genes (ND4, ND6) and complex I deficiency in one family. It describes this as a 'link', not as proof that the disorder in general is caused by these mutations.

checks.claim: A mutation in the MTND6 gene has been suggested as the disease-causing mutation in several families with Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
checks.explanation: NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 is MTND6, and the paper says the mutation was suggested as causative in several families.

paragraphs.text: Novotny et al. (1986) studied a large kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber disease and 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration. One member had both disorders.

checks.claim: Novotny et al. (1986) studied a large kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber disease.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease
checks.explanation: The abstract says "a kindred" rather than "large kindred". However, 23 affected members implies a large kindred.

checks.claim: In the large kindred studied by Novotny et al. (1986), 14 members had a progressive, generalized dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration
checks.explanation: The count (14) and the description of the dystonia match the abstract.

checks.claim: The progressive generalized dystonia in the kindred studied by Novotny et al. (1986) was attributed to striatal degeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration
checks.explanation: The abstract attributes the dystonia to striatal degeneration.

checks.claim: One member of the kindred studied by Novotny et al. (1986) had both Leber neuroretinopathy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: and 1 had both disorders.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that one member had both disorders.

paragraphs.text: Marsden et al. (1986) reported familial dystonia with visual failure. Affected individuals had bilateral striatal lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen.

checks.claim: Marsden et al. (1986) reported familial dystonia with visual failure.
checks.evidence_quote: A unique disorder is described in seven members of two families in whom dystonia was variably associated with subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy
checks.explanation: The title, 'Familial dystonia and visual failure with striatal CT lucencies', and the abstract both describe familial dystonia with visual failure.

checks.claim: Individuals affected by familial dystonia with visual failure reported by Marsden et al. (1986) had bilateral striatal lucencies on CT scan.
checks.evidence_quote: striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen
checks.explanation: The abstract reports bilateral symmetrical CT lucencies, and the title calls them striatal.

checks.claim: The bilateral striatal lucencies on CT in the patients reported by Marsden et al. (1986) especially involved the putamen.
checks.evidence_quote: striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen
checks.explanation: The abstract says the lucencies especially involved the putamen.

paragraphs.text: In the kindred reported by Novotny et al. (1986), the mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission, and the authors suggested that the disorder may be a mitochondrial disease. Jun et al. (1994) found an mtDNA mutation in 6 maternal relatives in 3 generations of a family, 1 of whom was heteroplasmic. This confirmed transmission through the maternal line.

checks.claim: In the kindred reported by Novotny et al. (1986), the mode of inheritance of Leber optic atrophy and dystonia was compatible with maternal transmission.
checks.evidence_quote: The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Novotny et al. (1986) suggested that Leber optic atrophy and dystonia may be a mitochondrial disease.
checks.evidence_quote: This neurologic disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.
checks.explanation: The authors suggest the disorder may be mitochondrial.

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1994) found an mtDNA mutation in 6 maternal relatives in 3 generations of a family with Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation
checks.explanation: Six maternal relatives in three generations carried the mutation.

checks.claim: One of the 6 maternal relatives carrying the mtDNA mutation in the family studied by Jun et al. (1994) was heteroplasmic.
checks.evidence_quote: with one female affected with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy being heteroplasmic
checks.explanation: One relative, a female with LHON, was heteroplasmic.

checks.claim: The findings of Jun et al. (1994) confirmed transmission of Leber optic atrophy and dystonia through the maternal line.
checks.evidence_quote: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia
checks.explanation: The abstract describes maternal transmission and finds the mutation in maternal relatives. The word 'confirmed' is the draft's interpretation of these statements.

paragraphs.text: Jun et al. (1994) studied a 5-generation Hispanic family with maternally transmitted LHON and/or early-onset dystonia. In the MTND6 gene they found a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459, which changes alanine to valine at residue 72 (A72V). The mutation segregated through the maternal line and was associated with both LHON and dystonia.

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1994) studied a 5-generation Hispanic family with maternally transmitted LHON and/or early-onset dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions was studied.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In the 5-generation Hispanic family with LHON and/or dystonia, Jun et al. (1994) found a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 in the MTND6 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: One of these variants, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459, changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72.
checks.explanation: ND6 is the same gene as MTND6.

checks.claim: The MTND6 14459G-A transition changes alanine to valine at residue 72 (A72V).
checks.evidence_quote: changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72
checks.explanation: Alanine to valine at residue 72 is the same as A72V.

checks.claim: The MTND6 14459G-A mutation segregated through the maternal line in the Hispanic family studied by Jun et al. (1994).
checks.evidence_quote: Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation
checks.explanation: The mutation was found in maternal relatives across three generations, which shows it passed through the maternal line.

checks.claim: The MTND6 14459G-A mutation was associated with both LHON and dystonia in the Hispanic family studied by Jun et al. (1994).
checks.evidence_quote: A mitochondrial DNA mutation at nucleotide pair 14459 of the NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 gene associated with maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia.
checks.explanation: The title links the mutation to both LHON and dystonia. The abstract does not break this down by individual carrier.

paragraphs.text: De Vries et al. (1996) studied a large Dutch family with LHON associated with hereditary spastic dystonia. Affected members carried the 11696 mutation in the MTND4 gene together with a mutation at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene.

checks.claim: De Vries et al. (1996) studied a large Dutch family with LHON associated with hereditary spastic dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: A rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) that is associated with hereditary spastic dystonia has been studied in a large Dutch family.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Dutch family studied by De Vries et al. (1996) carried the 11696 mutation in the MTND4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports the 11696 ND4 mutation (heteroplasmic) but does not say which family members, or that all affected members, carried it. That detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Dutch family studied by De Vries et al. (1996) carried a mutation at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene together with the MTND4 11696 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: A second mutation, a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene, resulted in the substitution of a methionine for the isoleucine at amino acid residue 26.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports the 14596 ND6 mutation alongside the 11696 mutation but does not say that affected members carried both. That detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Bilateral striatal lucencies on CT; striatal degeneration
